headline: High-risk default workspace overlap: Roo Code can write shared files and use MCP/browser tools, while ComfyUI is offline-only but can still be steered through shared artifacts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists if Roo Code reads ComfyUI-generated files or workflow artifacts as instructions, because ComfyUI exposes files/workflows and Roo Code can read workspace files and use MCP/browser tools. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high, but the shared-file pathway is credible.
conditions: IF Roo Code ingests ComfyUI output files or workflow JSON as trusted instructions
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or shared directory
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate directory from Roo Code workspaces
Disable automatic parsing of generated files in Roo Code
Require manual review before any MCP action triggered by file contents
Use read-only mounts for ComfyUI output folders
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between generated artifacts and agent inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files and send context to configured model APIs, while ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts. If sensitive media or checkpoints are placed in a shared workspace, Roo Code may transmit them off-box; ComfyUI itself is offline-only, so the main leakage risk is through Roo Code.
conditions: IF sensitive images, videos, or model artifacts are stored in a workspace readable by Roo Code
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace context to a third-party model API
mitigations: Store sensitive media outside any Roo Code workspace
Use a local-only model backend for Roo Code
Redact or exclude large binary files from context collection
Restrict workspace permissions to least privilege
requires-engineering: add file-type allowlists for context upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has filesystem write, shell, git, and MCP capabilities, while ComfyUI can operate on files and workflows. In a shared workspace, Roo Code can overwrite or mutate artifacts ComfyUI depends on, and the pair lacks documented locking or coordination. That makes default concurrent use dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree
IF Roo Code edits files that ComfyUI reads or writes during the same session
mitigations: Separate ComfyUI and Roo Code into different directories
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts
Use git branches or copies instead of a shared working tree
Make ComfyUI outputs read-only to Roo Code
requires-engineering: add workspace locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on file contents and MCP/browser outputs, so if it consumes ComfyUI-generated prompts, captions, or workflow metadata as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code or actions. ComfyUI does not verify downstream use, and Roo Code’s approval-per-tool model reduces but does not eliminate this pathway.
conditions: IF Roo Code treats ComfyUI-generated artifacts as factual input without verification
IF Roo Code uses those artifacts to drive code changes or browser actions
mitigations: Require explicit verification before Roo Code acts on ComfyUI outputs
Label ComfyUI artifacts as untrusted in the workspace
Insert a human review step for any downstream action
Keep generated media and instructions in separate folders
requires-engineering: add schema validation for workflow handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. ComfyUI is offline-only and Roo Code’s compliance surface is mainly its configured model provider and workspace handling, so only a limited compliance gap is visible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Roo Code is configured to send regulated data to a provider lacking the required controls
IF regulated media is placed in a workspace that Roo Code uploads or logs
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Roo Code workspaces
Use a provider with the required compliance posture
Disable retention where the provider allows it
Review logging settings before use
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency boundaries
